summary: Site Diary V2 iteration-19 (reordered 11-step wizard + Actions register + dual sign-off + priority/breakdown/details + weather+user filters + outstandingActions stat) tested end-to-end. Backend: 19/19 pytest passing (all previous iteration-18 regressions plus 6 new tests covering actions[], completedBy/Signature, supervisorName/Signature, delays[].priority, plant[].breakdown, worksCompleted[].details, and stats.outstandingActions counting logic incl. exclusion of Done/Complete/Completed/Closed). Frontend: all requested selectors present — 6 dashboard stat cards including sd-stat-actions, sd-filter-weather & sd-filter-user; wizard opens with 11-step stepper in the exact reordered sequence (Project→Weather→Labour→Works→Deliveries→Plant→Delays→Variations→Photos→Actions→Sign-off); Step 1 exposes sd-completedBy alongside date/start/end/link-project; Step 2 (Weather) confirmed to have NO date/start/end fields inside sd-step-2-weather wrapper (JS scope check returned {date:false,start:false,end:false}); Step 4 shows sd-work-details-1 textarea; Step 6 shows sd-plant-breakdown-1 select; Step 7 shows sd-delay-priority-1 select; Step 10 is sd-step-10-actions with sd-action-add and per-row description/responsible/dueDate/priority/status; Step 11 is sd-step-11-signoff with both sd-sign-completed and sd-sign-supervisor buttons that open sd-sign-modal independently (Supervisor Signature title confirmed via screenshot). No regressions.
critical_code_review_comments: site_diary.py cleanly adds new fields to both EntryIn and EntryUpdate; stats.outstandingActions correctly lowercases and excludes {done, complete, completed, closed} per spec.
SiteDiary.jsx (985 lines) is getting large — consider splitting into per-step components (StepProject/StepWeather/…/StepSignoff) into /pages/site-diary/steps/ for maintainability. Not blocking.
Backwards-compatibility fields (preparedBy, signature, linkedDocuments) are preserved and the sign-off flow writes completedSignature/supervisorSignature independently, matching the spec.
RowEditor generic component reuses column contract cleanly for the new priority/breakdown selects — good DRY.

Backend does not currently validate action.status enum values (accepts arbitrary strings) — non-blocking because stats lowercases and compares to a whitelist of closed states, but a Pydantic enum for status would harden the API.
